assessment.flow_conclusion: The reported flow runs from the zero-initialized salt buffer at line 188 to the KDF argument at line 210. It omits the intervening full-buffer write by decoded.read_exact(&mut salt)? at line 193. A short read returns an error before the KDF. Successful decryption uses the serialized salt; an all-zero input salt would be input data, not this initializer surviving unchanged.
assessment.encryption_countercheck: encrypt_helper calls rng.fill_bytes(&mut salt) at line 163 before its KDF at line 165.
assessment.qualification: This resolves the flagged initializer-to-KDF path only; it is not a general cryptographic review or native test run.

findings.message: This operation dereferences a pointer that may be [invalid](1).

assessment.flow_conclusion: The reported path starts at null_mut and jumps to read_unaligned. Actual source calls GetAce with &mut ace, rejects failed GetAce or a null result, and checks the requested span against a validated live ACL before the read. The unchanged-null path shown by the SARIF cannot reach the read through these guards. Source inspection also checked allocation lifetime and full bounds, rather than assuming non-null implies validity.
guard_and_lifetime_reasoning: GetSecurityInfo requests OWNER and DACL, requires ERROR_SUCCESS and non-null descriptor/owner/dacl at253-276.
The returned descriptor allocation remains live through the entire synchronous DACL inspection; LocalFree occurs at282 after inspection, not before.
IsValidAcl succeeds and GetAclInformation(AclSizeInformation) supplies AclBytesInUse before enumeration at289-309.
Each GetAce must return success and a non-null pointer at327-332.
ace_span_fits_acl validates the requested header span at333-340; its checked_add arithmetic rejects overflow, pointers before the first ACE, and spans beyond bytes in use at384-402.
ptr::read_unaligned copies a value without creating a misaligned Rust reference.
assessment.qualification: Conclusion relies on the documented Win32 success/out-parameter/allocation contracts. No native Windows execution was performed and no alert state is changed.
